description: House layout: permanent grid addresses for recurring operational and repair words. Addresses are 1-based [row, column] and are computed from the grid size, so Help is always the bottom-left cell, Finished the bottom-right, and so on. Every board page must place these words at their house address; a word keeps its address for life. Grow a board by hiding cells in place (button.hidden), never by reshuffling.

different.note: 'Not that' family: Different on talking pages, Undo on message pages, Delete on keyboard pages. Grids with fewer than 3 columns have no different slot.

finished.note: Finished on talking pages; Start again (clear) on message pages.

stop.note: Top-right is the voice corner: the Stop word, or Speak on message pages. The runtime's Stop speech control appears just beside it in the reserved edge column.

nav.note: The forward page button ('<next page> ▶'). On grids with fewer than 3 rows it shares the top-right cell with the stop slot.

keyboard.note: ABC: opens the spelling keyboard from the first page. Shares its cell with nav-back, which only appears on later pages. Grids with fewer than 3 rows use the top-left cell.

nav-back.note: '◀ previous page' on talking pages after the first, so neighbouring pages are one step apart. Same cell as ABC on the first page.

positionKeywords.middle: ceil(n / 2): row 2 of 3 or 4, column 2 of 3 or 4, column 3 of 5 or 6

contentRules: Content words fill the remaining cells in reading order.
A reserved cell whose house word is absent from the page may hold content, except the Help cell (validator warning).
Talking pages are linked in a ring: one forward button per page (nav) plus a back button (nav-back) on talking pages after the first. Generated core-word and word-ending pages are forward-only.
Two words from the same slot on one page is a conflict: split the page or drop one.
Grids smaller than 2x2 have no house template; the validator warns.
